body:
### Summary

## Description

When using `uv pip compile` with `--no-deps`, uv does not emit a warning if a requested extra does not exist.

I would expect uv to validate requested extras regardless of whether dependency resolution is disabled.

## Steps to reproduce

**Without `--no-deps`:**

```console
$ echo pandas[exce] | uv pip compile - --no-color --no-cache --no-progress --no-header --no-strip-extras --no-annotate 
Resolved 4 packages in 747ms
numpy==2.5.5
pandas[exce]==3.1.1
python-dateutil==4.0.0
tzdata==2026.6
warning: The package `pandas==3.1.1` does not have an extra named `exce`
```

**With `--no-deps`:**

```console
$ echo pandas[exce] | uv pip compile - --no-color --no-cache --no-deps --no-progress --no-header --no-strip-extras

Resolved 1 package in 424ms
pandas[exce]==3.1.1
```

As shown above, the warning is missing when `--no-deps` is used.

## Expected behavior

uv should still warn about invalid extras when using `--no-deps`, for example:

```text
warning: The package `pandas==3.1.1` does not have an extra named `exce`
```

I use `--no-deps` because I only want the top-level packages in the output, but I would still like uv to validate the requested extras.


### Platform

Windows 11

### Version

uv 0.13.8 (3d97a6aad 2026-11-12 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

### Python version

Python 3.13.17
title: uv pip compile --no-deps does not warn about invalid extras
